messages:
anya: Heads-up from this morning's canary: we still saw duplicated provisional tokens when streaming requests hit regional fallback + reconnects. Patterns differ from earlier incidents  this one's cross-region so provenance is weaker.
sam: cross-region makes sense. orig_session headers aren't always propagated across regions for latency reasons. Any logs?
kevin: snippet: 
```
[2025-09-14T08:12:01Z] session=rt-44 region=us-east route=canary cb=tripped
[2025-09-14T08:12:02Z] client reconnect session=rt-44b region=eu-west orig_session=rt-44? (missing)
[2025-09-14T08:12:03Z] toolcall id=tool-embed status=ok chunk=1 tokens=45
[2025-09-14T08:12:03Z] billing provisional session=rt-44 tokens=45
[2025-09-14T08:12:04Z] billing provisional session=rt-44b tokens=44
```
maria: If orig_session isn't reliably set across region handoffs we can't dedupe on session_origin alone. We should consider a merge_score in reconciler that combines provenance signals rather than binary link.
anya: I like that. Score inputs: session_origin presence (high weight), request_id match (high), fingerprint match of chunk (medium), time_delta (inverse weight), client_account match (mandatory). Based on score threshold we auto-merge or surface to ops.
sam: Important: never auto-refund on borderline scores. Maybe two-tier: score >= 0.9 -> auto-merge+auto-refund; 0.6-0.9 -> flagged merge (reconciler emits merge_id+reason but Billing holds until manual approval or delayed auto-refund); <0.6 -> no merge.
kevin: Implementation: reconciler produces merge_candidate with fields: merge_id, score (0-1), evidence list (strings). We'll keep evidence as simple tags (ORIGIN_MATCH, FINGERPRINT_EQ, TIME_LT_120s, TOKEN_DELTA_SMALL). Billing API: POST /internal/billing/merge_proposal {merge_id, sessions, merged_tokens, score, evidence}. Billing decides action based on score + throttles.
lucy: Console UX: show "merge candidates" in Cost Explorer with color-coded severity: auto-applied (green), pending approval (amber), rejected (gray). For pending, provide a one-click "Approve refund" for support ops with audit trail. Also add a small explanatory tooltip about scoring heuristic.
maria: Telemetry required: reconciler.merge_candidates_total, reconciler.merged_auto_total, reconciler.merged_manual_total, reconciler.merge_score_distribution, reconciler.merge_evidence_counts. Also crosslink to traces: include trace_id in evidence so ops can inspect.
anya: Rollout plan: add reconciler.merge_scoring behind feature flag reconciler.merge_score_v1. Start with read-only mode (score computed + candidate posted to /internal/merge-log but Billing not called) for 48h. Monitor score distribution and false-positive rate by sampling manual reviews.
esam: We'll need a manual review workflow: small ops UI that surfaces pending candidates with quick trace links, tokens delta, sessions, score, and approve/deny buttons. Lucy, can you add that to Console support panel?
lucy: yes. UI will show candidate list, filters by account, score range, and a preview of pre-merge provisional lines. Approve flow calls Billing endpoint to execute merge. We'll add audit entries in Console and a short note in cost timeline: "Merged provisional tokens (auto/manual)".
kevin: Edge case: model-quantization differences across regions can change token counts; fingerprinting should include model_id+model_checksum where available, but checksum may differ if models are hot-swapped. We'll make fingerprint optional and penalize score when missing.
maria: Also enforce policy: never merge across different customer_account ids. That prevents cross-tenant collapse.
billing-bot: Finance policy: auto-refund allowed for merges with merged_value_usd <= 1000 and daily_auto_refund_total <= 20k. We'll reject auto-refund beyond those thresholds and route to manual queue. Billings will accept merge proposal with score and decide. We'll emit billing.merge_action events.
anya: For rollouts, include a rollback affordance in the Console: if a daily false-positive rate > 0.5% in first 24h, auto-disable reconciler.merge_score_v1. We'll surface that metric on rollout card.
esam: Tests: unit tests for scoring function, integration sim cross-region reconnect+tool truncation with/without fingerprints, e2e for Console approve flow. We'll also simulate high-volume duplicates to test billing throttle.
kevin: Implementation tasks: reconciler: compute score + evidence, emit candidate to merge-log, endpoint to POST to billing. Billing: accept merge_proposal and apply/refuse based on policy and throttles. Console: candidate drawer + approve/deny flows + rollout card. Ops: runbook for manual refunds and revert.
maria: One more telemetry ask: correlate merge candidates to customer support tickets by tagging candidate with potential-srgb label. We'll add candidate tags and a short webhook to create a support task when score in [0.6,0.9).
lucy: UX note: keep text concise. Example tooltip: "Score is heuristic combining session origin, request id, content fingerprint, and timing. Higher score = higher confidence this is a duplicate provisional."
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: reconciler-merge-score-v1 -> canary-cluster -> 2025-09-15T02:00Z. /deploy reconciler-merge-score-v1
anya: OK. I'll monitor merge_score_distribution and reconciler.merged_manual_total during canary. If manual approvals are frequent we'll tighten threshold.
sam: ping finance if we hit billing.merge_action=auto_refund > 50 in 1h during rollout.
billing-bot: noted. Will enforce initial throttle 5/min and daily cap 20k USD.
anya: Thanks all. I'll open a short runbook and link it here with rollback steps and how to triage borderline merges.
kevin: PRs incoming: reconciler scoring + merge-log writer; billing merge API + policy layer; console candidate drawer. ETA: 3 days for core reconciler + 1 day for console mock.
maria: thanks, will help tune scoring weights after first telemetry run.
lucy: will mock the UI today and share in #design.
sam: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
